### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**11** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `563ef9ed548df57cfbc9f9e324dd7e2d73ebcab8` — the merge of head `b30e9bb456b6a423e09b5e76a00d80044fc5dbc0` into base `6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 563ef9ed548df57cfbc9f9e324dd7e2d73ebcab8 && git checkout 563ef9ed548df57cfbc9f9e324dd7e2d73ebcab8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3 b30e9bb456b6a423e09b5e76a00d80044fc5dbc0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3 && git merge --no-ff b30e9bb456b6a423e09b5e76a00d80044fc5dbc0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e1cae2e5934b1b05dbe9c678c154d34b7fdb6f8a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts (read only)

### ① Derived judgments

- The decision order in `routeHolderCensus` (1 disabled-only on the route → none; 2 environment's item on the first rung; 3 one served package on the first rung, no platform item → that package's exact-address read, served unqualified; else the bare read) matches the FROM→TO table, and each row is pinned in both registration orders. `environmentOwnerOfUnheldRoute` keeps main's answer through the shared reader. The `_env` 404 branch only answers the environment's own item from the store-checked rung, never a package's or the platform's. Refusals of the exact-address read fall back to the bare read; other throws are `degraded` (ADR-0110 D3). Correct.
- **must-fix M1 — the census reads the environment store on every dispatch of a package-less action, before it knows the census applies.** `resolveRouteActionDeclaration` now calls `routeHolderCensus` after every successful bare read (before this PR the shared reader ran only on the refused-read path). `readRouteHolders` runs `environmentStoredActionNames(ql)()` (full `sys_metadata` reads of every active `action` and `object` row, JSON-parsing each, plus the legacy-row read) whenever ANY package-less item owns the route, and only afterwards does `routeHolderCensus` apply its guards (`!named.some(packagedItem)` → bare read). Consequences:
  1. Hot path: every call of a host/plugin action or an environment-authored action (the one-holder, no-package case, i.e. most actions) pays two-plus table scans per request.
  2. Red line "phase-1 one-holder behaviour unchanged": if that store read throws, a one-holder platform or environment action that dispatched on `main` now answers `degraded`. One-holder dispatch now depends on a read it did not use before.
  Fix: read the listing first and apply the composition guards (a packaged item in `named`, AND a package-less item or a disabled package) before touching the store; read the store only when the census can still answer, and only for rules 1/2/3 that need it. Add a pin: one holder (platform item, and environment item) with a store whose `find` throws still dispatches as on BASE, and a counting `find` shows no store read for a one-holder name.
- nit N1: `registry.listItems('action', undefined, { includeDisabledPackages: true })` now runs per dispatch too and filters every action by name; with M1's guard it at least short-circuits cheaply. A by-name holder read (`packageScopedHoldersOf`) would be cheaper if the registry offers one; optional.
- Not fixed here, correctly surfaced: #32996 item 2 (one package-less slot per name in `registry.ts`) needs a decision; the released CHANGELOG sentence (#32995 item 3) is owed as a docs-only PR. Both should be on the seat's list.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime: patch` with `fix(runtime)!` and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (one narrowing row: environment item beside a disabled route holder and one enabled holder elsewhere → no declaration; the rest widen) is right. No export or schema moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. `Skills-docs: none — REASON` acceptable.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Hot path: `/api/v1/actions/**` dispatch (see M1).
- Author login `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); area E2b session_016WV4cyWLSMyXZGc6dwhCAu. Shared file owner per amendment 6: `packages/runtime` action routes = E2b; check A5 has no open PR on `action-execution.ts` before landing.
- PR body says verification readings live in the `os-dev-report` on #32996; the ACCEPT must re-read checks at the landing head.

### ④ Design judgment

Answering the bare route from who holds the name on the route, instead of from a by-name read that cannot see the object, is the right model for ADR-0150 D3/D4 and removes the registration-order dependence the cards describe. The narrowing row is main's own answer applied consistently and is declared. The design fails only on cost and isolation: the census must not touch the store, or change any outcome, for compositions it does not decide. With M1 fixed and pinned this is PASS.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b30e9bb456b6a423e09b5e76a00d80044fc5dbc0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts

Delta over my FAIL at `e1cae2e5934b1b05dbe9c678c154d34b7fdb6f8a` (comment 6879733874). The diff `e1cae2e5...b30e9bb4` is one commit, two files, +55/-6.

### ① Derived judgments

- **M1 fixed.** `readRouteHolders` now takes an `admit(named, isDisabled)` predicate that it asks of the registry listing before `environmentStoredActionNames(ql)` runs, and it answers `undefined` with no store read when `admit` refuses. `routeHolderCensus` passes exactly the two guards it used to apply after the read: some package holder, and either a package-less holder or a disabled one beside it. The decided compositions are therefore unchanged, and every other composition takes the bare read without touching the store. `isDisabled` is built before `admit` from the registry alone, so the predicate needs no store state. The default `admit` (`() => true`) keeps any other caller of `readRouteHolders` as it was.
- **Pins.** For each one-holder shape (only the environment's item, only the platform's item, one package's item): with a store whose `find` throws, the route answers that holder and the call dispatches, so it is never `degraded`; and with a counting store, the route makes zero `sys_metadata` reads. These pin both halves of M1 (cost and outage isolation).
- Residual, accepted: a mixed composition (a package holder beside a package-less or disabled one) still reads the store per dispatch. That is the composition the census exists to decide. N1 (by-name holder listing instead of `listItems` + filter) stays optional.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from the first record: `@objectstack/runtime: patch`, `fix(runtime)!`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- CI at this head when read (17:41Z): 3 success, 16 skipped, 20 in progress, **1 failure**: `PR-body guards` — "PR #33274 closes #32995, #32989, #32988 with no `Claim:` on the card naming `claude/area-E2b-32996`". This is a process gate on the folded cards' claims, not code. It must be green (claims posted on the three cards via fleet-write) before the ACCEPT.
- The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.

### ④ Design judgment

Unchanged: answering the bare route from who holds the name on the route is the right model for ADR-0150 D3/D4. With the census now consulting the store only for the compositions it decides, its cost and failure stay inside those compositions. One-holder behaviour is unchanged in both outcome and cost. The design holds.

Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6`

**VERDICT: PASS**

    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/client:test: Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
